story_description: Establish foundational communication layer between Blaze and the Codex app-server daemon, enabling JSON-RPC based interaction for advanced scenarios where the app-server mode provides better session management and event streaming than direct CLI invocation.
task_description: Create CodexAppServerAdapter class that handles JSON-RPC 2.0 communication with the Codex app-server daemon, including connection management, request/response serialization, notification handling, and error propagation.
atom_description: Implement CodexAppServerAdapter actor conforming to EngineAdapter protocol with JSON-RPC 2.0 client capabilities over HTTP transport, including request ID generation, response correlation, notification stream handling, and comprehensive error types for connection failures, timeouts, and protocol errors.
problem_statement: Codex CLI can run in app-server mode which provides a persistent daemon process with JSON-RPC interface. This offers advantages over direct CLI spawning: persistent sessions, better event streaming, and reduced process overhead. However, Blaze currently has no adapter to communicate with this mode. We need a robust JSON-RPC client adapter that can connect to the app-server, send requests, receive responses, and handle the bidirectional notification stream for real-time updates.

scope_out: App-server process lifecycle management (covered in X002-MANAGER)

assumptions: Codex app-server runs on localhost at a configurable port (default 3333)
App-server implements JSON-RPC 2.0 specification over HTTP POST
App-server provides SSE endpoint for notification streaming at /events
All communication is unencrypted over localhost (no TLS required)
App-server is single-tenant, no multi-user authentication needed
Response timeout of 30 seconds is acceptable for most operations
URLSession is appropriate for HTTP transport (no need for custom networking)
Swift Concurrency (async/await, actors) is the preferred concurrency model
constraints: Must conform to existing EngineAdapter protocol for integration with SessionStore
Actor isolation required to prevent data races on connection state
All network operations must be cancellable via Task cancellation
Error messages must be user-readable for display in UI
No third-party dependencies allowed; use Foundation networking only
Must support macOS 13.0+ (Ventura) minimum deployment target
JSON encoding/decoding must handle all Codable types in request params
Notification stream must not block the main thread
functional_requirements: FR1: CodexAppServerAdapter shall conform to EngineAdapter protocol with async methods for submit, cancel, and event stream
FR2: Adapter shall implement JSON-RPC 2.0 request format with id (String), jsonrpc (literal 2.0), method (String), params (Encodable?)
FR3: Adapter shall parse JSON-RPC 2.0 response format with id, result (Decodable), or error (code, message, data)
FR4: Adapter shall maintain a dictionary mapping request IDs to CheckedContinuation for response correlation
FR5: Adapter shall generate unique request IDs using UUID().uuidString for each outgoing request
FR6: Adapter shall provide connect() async throws method to establish HTTP connection and verify server availability
FR7: Adapter shall provide disconnect() method to close connections and cancel pending requests
FR8: Adapter shall expose connectionState: ConnectionState published property for UI binding
FR9: Adapter shall provide call<T: Decodable>(method: String, params: Encodable?) async throws -> T for generic RPC calls
FR10: Adapter shall provide notifications: AsyncStream<JSONRPCNotification> property for incoming notifications
FR11: Adapter shall timeout requests after configurable duration (default 30 seconds) with TimeoutError
FR12: Adapter shall propagate JSON-RPC error responses as CodexRPCError with code, message, and optional data
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Request round-trip latency shall be under 100ms for local requests (excluding server processing)
NFR2: Adapter shall support at least 10 concurrent pending requests without degradation
NFR3: Memory footprint of adapter instance shall not exceed 1MB excluding response buffers
NFR4: Notification stream shall deliver events within 50ms of server emission
NFR5: Connection establishment shall complete within 5 seconds or fail with timeout
NFR6: Adapter shall gracefully handle server disconnect without crashing
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file CodexAppServerAdapter.swift in Blaze/Sources/Engine/ directory
Step 2: Define ConnectionState enum with cases: disconnected, connecting, connected, error(Error)
Step 3: Define JSONRPCRequest struct with id (String), jsonrpc (String = 2.0), method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
Step 4: Define JSONRPCResponse<T: Decodable> struct with id (String), result (T?), error (JSONRPCError?)
Step 5: Define JSONRPCError struct with code (Int), message (String), data (AnyCodable?)
Step 6: Define JSONRPCNotification struct with method (String), params (AnyCodable?)
Step 7: Define CodexRPCError enum with cases: connectionFailed(Error), timeout, invalidResponse(String), rpcError(JSONRPCError), serverDisconnected
Step 8: Declare CodexAppServerAdapter actor with @Published connectionState property

Step 9: Add stored properties: baseURL (URL), session (URLSession), pendingRequests ([String: CheckedContinuation<Data, Error>]), notificationContinuation (AsyncStream<JSONRPCNotification>.Continuation?)
Step 10: Implement init(host: String, port: Int) initializer with URL construction and URLSession configuration
Step 11: Implement connect() async throws that performs health check request to /health endpoint
Step 12: Implement disconnect() that cancels all pending requests and closes notification stream
Step 13: Implement private sendRequest<P: Encodable, R: Decodable>(method: String, params: P?) async throws -> R
Step 14: Implement request timeout using withTimeout or Task.sleep + cancellation check
Step 15: Implement startNotificationStream() that opens SSE connection to /events endpoint
Step 16: Implement private parseSSELine(_ line: String) -> JSONRPCNotification? for SSE parsing
Step 17: Implement call<T: Decodable>(method: String, params: Encodable?) async throws -> T public API
Step 18: Implement EngineAdapter protocol methods delegating to call() with appropriate method names
Step 19: Add comprehensive documentation comments for all public types and methods
Step 20: Write unit tests with mock URLProtocol for HTTP responses

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Server not running when connect() called - throws connectionFailed with ECONNREFUSED underlying error
Edge case 2: Server crashes mid-request - pending continuation resumed with serverDisconnected error
Edge case 3: Response received for unknown request ID - logged as warning, response discarded
Edge case 4: Malformed JSON in response body - throws invalidResponse with parsing error details
Edge case 5: Server returns JSON-RPC error response - throws rpcError with code and message
Edge case 6: Request cancelled by Task cancellation - continuation cancelled, request removed from pending
Edge case 7: Multiple rapid connect() calls - only first proceeds, subsequent await first completion
Edge case 8: SSE stream interrupted - notification continuation finishes, triggers reconnect via manager
Edge case 9: Very large response body (over 10MB) - handled by URLSession memory limits, may fail
Edge case 10: Server returns success response with null result - decoded as nil, valid for void methods
failure_modes: FM1: ECONNREFUSED on connect - display Connection refused error with suggestion to start app-server
FM2: Request timeout after 30 seconds - display timeout error, allow retry
FM3: JSON decode failure - display Invalid response from server with raw response in logs
FM4: RPC error code -32600 (Invalid Request) - display Server rejected request, check parameters
FM5: RPC error code -32601 (Method not found) - display Method not supported by app-server version
FM6: RPC error code -32603 (Internal error) - display Server internal error, check server logs
FM7: SSL/TLS error (if HTTPS attempted) - should not occur on localhost, fallback to HTTP
FM8: Memory pressure during large response - URLSession handles, may receive didReceiveMemoryWarning
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerAdapter.swift file. Remove any imports of CodexAppServerAdapter from other files. The adapter is additive and has no persistent state, so removal is clean. No database migrations or user data affected.

notes: This adapter enables advanced Codex integration beyond simple CLI spawning. The app-server mode provides better performance for high-frequency interactions and persistent sessions. risks: Risk 1: Codex app-server API may change between versions, breaking adapter
Risk 2: JSON-RPC error codes from Codex may not match standard codes, causing incorrect error handling
Risk 3: SSE parsing may be fragile if server sends non-standard events
Risk 4: Actor isolation may cause unexpected suspension points during critical sections
Risk 5: URLSession may not handle SSE streaming optimally on macOS
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Version check on connect, warn user if version mismatch detected
Mitigation 2: Map all unknown error codes to generic rpcError case with raw code
Mitigation 3: Log unparseable SSE lines and skip rather than crash
Mitigation 4: Use sendable closures and minimize shared state in actor
Mitigation 5: Implement custom SSE parser if URLSession proves problematic
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to Codex app-server integration feature. Failure does not affect Claude or Gemini adapters. Users can fall back to direct CLI spawning mode for Codex.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If app-server integration proves unreliable, disable feature flag and use direct Codex CLI spawning via existing CodexCliAdapter. No user data affected as app-server state is ephemeral.
